295	## 5. SimPoint-driven mode - the whole program
296	
297	### What it does
298	
299	Real programs run billions of instructions; you cannot cycle-simulate all
300	of them. SimPoint samples instead: profile the run into fixed slices,
301	cluster the slices into a few representative phases, measure each phase like
302	icount mode, then weight-combine the per-phase cycles into a whole-program
303	estimate. SimPoint mode is icount mode applied at several clustering-chosen
304	points.
305	
306	### Stages
307	
308	1. **Profile (BBV).** The plugin emits one Basic-Block-Vector row per slice
309	   of N retired insns into a SimPoint `.bb` file (`bbv_out=`, `slice=N`).
310	2. **Cluster.** `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint` reads the `.bb` and clusters
311	   the rows into K representative phases: a `simpts` file (one slice index
312	   per cluster) and a `weights` file (one weight per cluster).
313	3. **Per phase.** For each representative slice K: QEMU drains at the end of
314	   slice K (`slice=N`, `slice_at=K`), vsim resumes and measures that slice's
315	   cycles (the `mcycle` delta).
316	4. **Archive / replay (optional).** A drained state plus its shared mmap can
317	   be packaged into `snap/K/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}` and replayed on
318	   another host. This is the checkpoint plumbing, not a separate mode.
319	5. **Combine.** `estimated_cycles = N_total * sum(weight_i * CPI_i)`, where
320	   `CPI_i = delta_mcycle_i / insns_measured` and `N_total` is the whole
321	   program's retired-instruction count.
322	
323	### Cycle figure (the headline)
324	
325	`hsim run --mode simpoint` runs every stage and prints the whole-program
326	number (and is aliased as `hsim estimate` for back-compat). Simpoint
327	always profiles to natural program exit, so the workload must be
328	markerless and must exit cleanly:
329	
330	```sh
331	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode simpoint \
332	  --interval 100 --max-k 2
333	```
334	
335	Last line:
336	
337	```
338	estimated_cycles=<N>  (N=<insns>, weighted_CPI=<x.xxx>)
339	```
340	
341	`N` is the true total retired-insn count, read from the plugin's atexit
342	counter. Run `./hsim run --help` for all flags.
343	
344	### Stage drill-downs
345	
346	Each stage also has a standalone subcommand, useful when debugging one
347	piece (the headline `--mode simpoint` strings them together):
348	
349	```sh
350	# Stage 1: profile (the lower-level `profile` subcommand DOES take
351	# --icount as a hard cap, since it is the standalone tool, not the
352	# simpoint pipeline which always runs to exit).
353	./hsim profile tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
354	  --slice 100 --icount 50000 -o /tmp/sp-profile.bb
355	
356	# Stage 2: cluster
357	./hsim cluster /tmp/sp-profile.bb --max-k 2 \
358	  --simpts /tmp/simpts --weights /tmp/weights
359	
360	# Stage 4: archive a drained state.bin + mmap pair, then replay it
361	./hsim archive --state /tmp/state.bin --mmap /tmp/share \
362	  --elf tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf -o /tmp/snap/0
363	./hsim replay /tmp/snap/0 --resume-with vsim
364	```
365	
366	### Headline command: the full loop

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
3	#
4	# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
5	# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
6	# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
7	# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
8	# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.
9	
10	# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
11	#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
12	#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
13	# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
14	# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
15	resolve_pc() {
16	  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
17	  case "$boundary" in
18	    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
19	    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
20	  esac
21	}
22	
23	# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
24	#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (defaulting to the planted
25	#   markers _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc), resolves each against
26	#   <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare hex). Returns 1
27	#   and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if either does not
28	#   resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message (default "pc").
29	roi_resolve_pair() {
30	  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
31	  local start="${ROI_START:-_hybrid_enter_pc}"
32	  local end="${ROI_END:-_hybrid_exit_pc}"
33	  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
34	  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
35	  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
36	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
37	    return 1
38	  fi
39	  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
40	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
41	    return 1
42	  fi
43	  return 0
44	}

63	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)

68	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()

84	QEMU1_RC=$?

90	fi
91	
92	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then

95	fi

97	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain + spawn QEMU 2"
98	set +e

100	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
101	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
102	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
103	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
104	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \

110	# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
111	# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
112	# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
113	# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
114	# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.

116	  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }

119	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
120	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")

122	  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
123	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
124	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
125	    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
126	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
127	      exit 1
128	    fi
129	    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
130	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
131	      exit 1
132	    fi
133	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
134	  fi
135	fi
136	
137	if [ "$RC" != "$EXPECT_RC" ]; then
138	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: expected exit $EXPECT_RC, got $RC"
139	  echo "--- sim log ---"
140	  cat "$SIM_LOG"
141	  exit 1
142	fi
143	
144	echo "[$FIXTURE 3/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] PASS: round-trip exit code $RC"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# RED->GREEN: resolve_pc maps an ROI boundary (a symbol name OR a 0x-hex
3	# address) to a bare hex address, resolving symbols against `nm` output.
4	# This is the primitive that lets pc mode point at ANY symbol/address
5	# instead of the planted _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc markers.
6	set -uo pipefail
7	
8	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
9	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/roi.sh"
10	
11	fail() { echo "FAIL[roi_resolve]: $1"; exit 1; }
12	
13	# Fake `nm --defined-only` output (columns: addr type name).
14	NM_FIXTURE='0000000000100002 T _hybrid_enter_pc
15	0000000000100020 T _hybrid_exit_pc
16	0000000000100040 T vmatmul_kernel
17	0000000000100000 T main'
18	
19	# 1. hex passthrough strips the 0x prefix, keeps the digits.
20	got=$(resolve_pc "0x100abc" "$NM_FIXTURE")
21	[ "$got" = "100abc" ] || fail "hex passthrough: want 100abc got '$got'"
22	
23	# 2. uppercase 0X prefix also stripped.
24	got=$(resolve_pc "0X1f" "$NM_FIXTURE")
25	[ "$got" = "1f" ] || fail "0X prefix: want 1f got '$got'"
26	
27	# 3. arbitrary symbol name resolves via nm output (not just the markers).
28	got=$(resolve_pc "vmatmul_kernel" "$NM_FIXTURE")
29	[ "$got" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "symbol resolve: want ...100040 got '$got'"
30	
31	# 4. the default marker symbol still resolves (backward compat).
32	got=$(resolve_pc "_hybrid_enter_pc" "$NM_FIXTURE")
33	[ "$got" = "0000000000100002" ] || fail "marker resolve: want ...100002 got '$got'"
34	
35	# 5. unknown symbol -> empty (caller turns this into a FAIL).
36	got=$(resolve_pc "nope" "$NM_FIXTURE")
37	[ -z "$got" ] || fail "unknown symbol: want empty got '$got'"
38	
39	# --- roi_resolve_pair: env defaulting + dual resolve, as e2e.sh uses it ---
40	
41	# 6. no ROI_START/ROI_END -> defaults to the planted marker symbols.
42	unset ROI_START ROI_END
43	roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t || fail "default pair: returned nonzero"
44	[ "$ENTER_PC" = "0000000000100002" ] || fail "default ENTER_PC: got '$ENTER_PC'"
45	[ "$EXIT_PC"  = "0000000000100020" ] || fail "default EXIT_PC: got '$EXIT_PC'"
46	
47	# 7. ROI_START symbol + ROI_END hex override the defaults.
48	ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END=0x100100 roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t \
49	  || fail "override pair: returned nonzero"
50	[ "$ENTER_PC" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "override ENTER_PC: got '$ENTER_PC'"
51	[ "$EXIT_PC"  = "100100" ]            || fail "override EXIT_PC: got '$EXIT_PC'"
52	
53	# 8. an unresolvable boundary fails loudly and names the offender.
54	out=$(ROI_START=ghost ROI_END=main roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" myfix 2>&1)
55	[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "bad start: expected nonzero return"
56	case "$out" in *"myfix"*"ghost"*) ;; *) fail "bad start: message missing label/symbol: '$out'";; esac
57	
58	echo "[roi_resolve] PASS"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
3	# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
4	# workspace.
5	#
6	# Env overrides:
7	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
8	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
9	#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
10	#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
11	#   MODE         csr | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
12	#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
13	#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
14	#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
15	#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
16	#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
17	#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 3 processes (qemu1, vsim, qemu2);
18	#                the headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's
19	#                own scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
20	#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)
21	
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
25	VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
26	HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
27	TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"
28	
29	VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
30	VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
31	if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
32	  VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
33	fi
34	
35	step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
36	ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
37	warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
38	fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
39	
40	require() {
41	  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
42	    fail "$1 not found: $2"
43	    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
44	    exit 1
45	  fi
46	}
47	require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
48	require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
49	require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"
50

50	
51	export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN
52	
53	REQUIRED_ELFS=(
54	  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
55	  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
56	  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
57	  rt_c_v_matmul
58	  # icount_spin: CSR-less spin loop. Used by switching-mode demos
59	  # T3/T4/T5/T7 (icount, BBV emit, slice-consume, SimPoint loop).
60	  icount_spin
61	)
62	need_build=0
63	for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
64	  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
65	done
66	if (( need_build )); then
67	  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
68	  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
69	fi
70	
71	# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
72	# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
73	# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
74	# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
75	RT_TESTS=(
76	  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip EXPECT_RC=3"
77	  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
78	  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
79	  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
80	  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
81	  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
82	  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
83	  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
84	  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
85	  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
86	  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
87	  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
88	  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
89	  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
90	  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
91	  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
92	  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
93	)
94	
95	NEG_TESTS=(
96	  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
97	  "rt_no_qemu_binary|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_no_qemu_binary.sh"
98	  "rt_gdbstub_timeout|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_gdbstub_timeout.sh"
99	  "rt_pty_handback|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_pty_handback.sh"
100	)
101	
102	MODE="${MODE:-both}"
103	case "$MODE" in
104	  csr|pc|both) ;;
105	  *) fail "MODE must be one of csr|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
106	esac
107	
108	default_jobs() {
109	  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
110	  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
111	  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
112	    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
113	    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
114	      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
115	      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
116	    fi
117	  fi
118	  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
119	  printf '%d\n' "$n"
120	}
121	JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
122	[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
123	  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }
124	
125	FILTER="${FILTER:-}"
126	
127	LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
128	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
129	RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
130	LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
131	: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
132	: > "$LOCK_FILE"
133	
134	# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
135	# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
136	# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
137	# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
138	# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
139	# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
140	# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
141	run_one() {
142	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
143	  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
144	  local start end elapsed status rc
145	  start=$(date +%s)
146	  set +e
147	  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
148	  rc=$?
149	  set -e
150	  end=$(date +%s)
151	  elapsed=$((end - start))
152	  case $rc in
153	    0)  status=PASS ;;
154	    77) status=SKIP ;;
155	    *)  status=FAIL ;;
156	  esac
157	  (
158	    flock 9
159	    case "$status" in
160	      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
161	      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
162	      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
163	    esac
164	    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
165	      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
166	  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
167	}
168	
169	# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
170	# matters: csr-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
171	# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
172	declare -a WORKPLAN=()
173	for tm in csr pc; do
174	  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
175	  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
176	    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
177	    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
178	    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ $FILTER ]] && continue
179	    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"

365	### 2.5 Requesting more memory (`--mmap-size` + `HSIM_MMAP_DIR`)
366

369	workload's memory footprint exceeds `/dev/shm` capacity (typically

439	## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use
440	
441	| Mode     | Profiles          | Switch boundary                                          | Cycle figure           |
442	|----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
443	| CSR      | a kernel          | `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` insn match (markers in source)         | kernel cycles          |

448	CSR/PC delimit ONE kernel you choose; icount/SimPoint sample the whole
449	program by instruction count (SimPoint is icount repeated, weight-combined).
450	How each is driven: every mode goes through `./hsim run --mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint`

452	the vsim `mcycle` delta (offset 624); SimPoint extrapolates many deltas

458	Profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?

464	  representative phases, combined  -> SimPoint  (./hsim run --mode simpoint)

719	#### Stage 4: `./hsim estimate` - whole-program cycle estimate (the headline)
720	
721	`./hsim run --mode simpoint <elf>` (or the equivalent `./hsim estimate
722	<elf>`) runs the full pipeline (BBV profile -> SimPoint cluster ->
723	per-phase QEMU+vsim drain) and aggregates a weighted CPI to project a

725	
726	```sh
727	./hsim run gemm.elf --mode simpoint --interval 5000 --max-k 4
728	# or, the lower-level alias:
729	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 5000 --max-k 4
730	```
731	
732	(`./hsim run --mode simpoint` uses `--interval`; `./hsim estimate` keeps
733	the historical `--slice` name. Both name the same "insns per slice"
734	parameter.)
735	
736	The profile pass **always runs the program to its natural exit** (e.g.
737	libgloss_vh semihosting EXIT). The plugin counts every retired insn via a
738	per-insn TCG callback and writes that count into the drained state file's
739	`minstret` field; hsim uses it as `N_total` in:
740	
741	```
742	CPI_i           = delta_mcycle_i / vsim_icount
743	weighted_CPI    = sum_i ( w_i * CPI_i )
744	estimated_cycles = N_total * weighted_CPI
745	```
746

760	- The fixture must reach `_exit` (return from `main`, or call `exit(0)`).
761	  Programs that hang in an infinite loop will hit the QEMU 30s profile
762	  timeout; simpoint mode is not designed for non-exiting workloads --
763	  cap them at the source or use a different mode (icount).
764	- The fixture must be **markerless** (no `csrwi 0x7C0,*`). The plugin's
765	  CSR matcher is still armed in simpoint mode and would drain at the
766	  first marker before natural exit, cutting `N_total` short.

771	#### How to pick `--slice` and `--max-k`
772	
773	These two flags trade profile granularity against vsim cost. Here is the
774	short version; the rest of this section explains why.
775	
776	```
777	slice  ~= N_total / 20         # aim for ~20 BBV rows
778	max-k  =  2                    # start simple, increase only if needed
779	```
780	
781	**Two-step workflow.** First run with defaults to learn N_total, then
782	re-run with a tuned slice:
783	
784	```sh
785	./hsim estimate myprog.elf
786	# read the line:  profile: <rows> BBV rows ... (N_total=<N>)
787	# then:
788	./hsim estimate myprog.elf --slice $((N/20))
789	```
790	
791	**Picking `--slice`** (insns per BBV row). One BBV row is the smallest
792	unit SimPoint can cluster. Too few rows -> k-means cannot find structure.
793	Too many rows -> long profile pass and long clustering. Aim for ~20.
794	
795	| Program size (N_total) | Pick `--slice`  |
796	|------------------------|-----------------|
797	| < 10K (toy)            | 500             |
798	| 10K..100K              | 1000..5000      |
799	| 100K..1M               | 5000..50000     |
800	| > 1M                   | 50000+          |
801	
802	**Picking `--max-k`** (number of phases). Each phase costs **one extra
803	QEMU+vsim drain pair** (~5..10s). SimPoint will sometimes pick fewer
804	phases than `--max-k` if the workload is uniform, so `max-k` is an upper
805	bound, not a fixed count.
806	
807	| Workload structure              | Pick `--max-k` |
808	|---------------------------------|----------------|
809	| Single loop kernel              | 2 (init + body) |
810	| Init + kernel + cleanup         | 3              |
811	| Multi-kernel (e.g. 2 GEMMs)     | 4..6           |
812	| Large benchmark mix             | 8..16          |
813	
814	**Sanity checks after a run.** Read the per-phase rows and apply:
815	
816	1. `BBV rows >= 2 * max_k`. If fewer, drop `--slice` so more rows fit.
817	2. Weights add to ~1.0 and are not all small. If all `--max-k` phases

1	# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises
2	
3	Status: draft for review
4	Audience: engineer running the hybrid co-simulator for the first time
5	Scope: the 4 switching modes the repo ships, with copy-paste commands,
6	the cycle figure each one yields, and one exercise per mode.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. What "switching mode" means
11	
12	The hybrid simulator runs a program across three phases:
13	
14	```
15	   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim  --(state file + same mmap)-->  QEMU2
16	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)                       (fast)
17	```
18	
19	A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN QEMU1 drains its
20	architectural state and hands the region of interest to vsim. vsim runs
21	that region cycle-accurately, then hands back to QEMU2 to finish. You pick
22	the rule with plugin args and vsim CLI flags; the fixture binary does not
23	have to change between modes.
24	
25	The repo ships **4 modes**, split by WHAT you profile.
26	
27	### Quick map
28	
29	| # | Mode | Profiles | Switch boundary | Cycle figure it yields |
30	|---|------|----------|-----------------|------------------------|
31	| 1 | CSR | a kernel | `csrwi 0x7C0,0` (enter) / `csrwi 0x7C0,1` (exit) | kernel cycles |
32	| 2 | PC | a kernel | a PC / symbol address (no source edit) | kernel cycles |
33	| 3 | icount | a sampled window | N retired insns (single boundary) | window cycles |
34	| 4 | SimPoint | the whole program | clustering picks representative slices | whole-program estimate |
35	
36	- **Kernel modes (CSR, PC)** measure ONE region you choose.
37	- **Whole-program modes (icount, SimPoint)** sample by instruction count.
38	  icount measures one window you place by hand; SimPoint measures several
39	  representative windows that clustering picks for you, then weight-combines
40	  them into a whole-program estimate. **SimPoint is just icount repeated.**
41	
42	(Migration: the old M1-M8 list collapses to these 4. Old M4-M7 are now
43	SimPoint stages; old M8 - QEMU2's semihosting exit - is the natural tail of
44	every run, not a selectable mode.)
45	
46	### Where the cycle figure comes from
47	
48	Every mode reads the same counter: `mcycle`, a little-endian `uint64` at
49	byte offset **624** in the state file (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). vsim
50	restores `mcycle` from QEMU1's drained value, then the RTL counts real
51	clock cycles, so the measured cycles are always a subtraction:
52	
53	```
54	cycles = mcycle(vsim drain) - mcycle(QEMU1 drain)
55	```
56	
57	The QEMU baseline cancels; only vsim's cycle-accurate delta survives. That
58	is why QEMU being functional-only (not cycle-accurate) does not taint the
59	number. CSR/PC/icount report this delta directly (kernel / window cycles);
60	SimPoint extrapolates many such deltas into a whole-program estimate
61	(Section 5).
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 1. One-time prerequisites
66	
67	Build everything once. Each command is idempotent.
68	
69	```sh
70	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
71	source ./setup.sh         # qemu + vsim + plugin + simpoint
72	```
73	
74	You should now have:
75	
76	| Artifact                                | Purpose                           |
77	|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
78	| `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`        | QEMU binary (phase 1 and phase 3) |
79	| `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`   | vsim binary (phase 2)             |
80	| `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`      | TCG plugin (state drainer)        |
81	| `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`           | SimPoint clustering tool (mode 4) |
82	| `tests/fixtures/*.elf`                  | Test fixtures (e.g. rt_c_v_matmul) |
83	
84	Common env vars (auto-detected by every demo; override only if you
85	keep these elsewhere):
86	
87	```sh
88	export VSIM_QEMU=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
89	export VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
90	export VSIM_BIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium

120	```
121	
122	Look for the two lines `qemu1: mcycle=...` and `vsim: mcycle=...`; the
123	kernel cycle count is `vsim - qemu1` (the GEMM kernel is ~22808 cycles).
124	
125	### Run it
126	
127	```sh
128	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
129	./hsim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode csr
130	```
131	
132	`hsim run --mode csr` is a thin Python wrapper around the generic harness
133	`tests/e2e.sh` (with `FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=csr`). Expected
134	last line: `PASS: round-trip exit code 0`.
135	
136	The plugin gets `outfile=<state.bin>` and nothing else - that is the CSR
137	default. vsim is launched without `--hybrid-exit-pc` and without
138	`--hybrid-icount`, so its ELF pre-scanner watches for `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` PCs
139	at retire.
140	
141	### Exercise 1
142	
143	The demos default to the GEMM, but the harness is fixture-parameterized -
144	switch from `rt_c_v_matmul` to `rt_c_matmul` (a scalar matmul) to confirm:
145	
146	```sh
147	FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=csr EXPECT_RC=0 CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1 \
148	  bash tests/e2e.sh
149	```
150	
151	Verify the last line says `PASS: round-trip exit code 0`, and note the
152	kernel cycle delta (smaller than the RVV GEMM's). Then read
153	`tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.c` and confirm where the two `csrwi 0x7C0, *`
154	markers live (`enter_vsim()` / `exit_vsim()` helpers).
155	
156	---
157	
158	## 3. PC mode - same kernel, no source edit
159	
160	### What it does
161	
162	Same round-trip as CSR mode, but the trigger is a PC value, not an opcode
163	match. The harness resolves each boundary - taken from `ROI_START` /
164	`ROI_END`, which default to the symbols `_hybrid_enter_pc` and
165	`_hybrid_exit_pc` - to an address (a `0x` value is used verbatim; a name is
166	looked up with `nm`, see `tests/lib/roi.sh`), then passes:
167	
168	- `enter_pc=0x<addr>` to the QEMU plugin (QEMU1 drains there)
169	- `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<addr>` to vsim (vsim drains there)
170	
171	CSR-mode matchers are bypassed; the `csrwi 0x7C0, *` instructions become
172	inert. This proves you can hand off WITHOUT modifying the source: point the
173	boundaries at any function or address the binary already has.
174	
175	### Inputs
176	
177	- Same fixture as CSR mode (`rt_c_v_matmul`). Both PC boundaries are
178	  **always explicit** -- pass `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (each a symbol
179	  name or `0x` address). There is no implicit fallback to planted
180	  `_hybrid_*_pc` markers.
181	
182	### Cycle figure
183	
184	Identical to CSR mode: kernel cycles = vsim `mcycle` - QEMU1 `mcycle`
185	(offset 624). The boundaries differ, the measurement does not. Underlying
186	harness invocation (the env-var form `hsim run --mode pc` forwards into):
187	
188	```sh
189	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=pc CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1 TIMEOUT=120 \
190	  ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END=0x<post-jal> \
191	  bash tests/e2e.sh
192	```

194	### Run it

198	  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x<post-jal>
199	```

201	### Drill-down
